newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds take back-seat to dlr,stocks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds take back-seat to dlr,stocks.

text.p: *Australian bonds spent another session rotating in a narrow range, taking a back-seat to the gyrations in both the local dollar and equities market.
*Monday's 3rd qtr capex data seen as next key event.
Australian bonds spent another session rotating in a narrow range, taking a back-seat to the gyrations in both the local dollar and equities market.

"For the first time in a while we are seeing physical stock coming back on to the market. We look fully priced on current fundamentals," one trader said. "Until we get some decent figures out we're looking pretty much stuck."

In the past 2-1/2 months the market has put in a solid rally, which has taken long-dated yields down some 100 basis points, but the approach to 7.0 percent on the benchmark 10-year bond is proving an extremely stiff barrier.

Meanwhile, the Australia dollar screeched to a six-year high against the U.S. dollar, breaching a key US$0.8050, while the All Ordinaries share index raced to an all time high of 2,406.2, at the opening, before retracing on profit-taking.
Until the bond market can build a solid case for a further easing in monetary policy, investors will be reluctant to push bond yields down much further, analysts said.

Three-year benchmark bond yields are currently glued to current 6.50 percent official interest rates, and for the 10-year yield to compress below 50 basis points to it is viewed too risky without any key data to ride on, they added.
The market how has to wait until Monday for the next key event when third quarter capital expediture is released, and more so the business investment intentions contained within it.
The Reserve Bank made a strong play on business investment in its quarterly bulletin last month in the country's push for growth, so a weak outcome could reignite thoughts of rate cut.

Meanwhile, the market faces further bond supply on Friday with Treasury Corp of Victoria (TCV) saying it will hold a tender. So far this week the market has absorbed supply from the Australian Treasury for fixed-interest and indexed stocks and from Queensland Treasury Corp (QTC).

Local bonds reversed the mild outperforming bias against other dollar bloc bonds with the market looking somewhat heavy going into the close. U.S. Treasuries held around Wednesday's yield lows during Tokyo trading.
